summary: Sequences are open (GenBank: 315,003 Foraminifera records, 2,387 matching SSU, 24 for Peneroplis, 501 for Soritidae; SRA 1,665; PR2 v5.1.1 release files) and planktonic shape images and morphometrics are open (Zenodo 165514, 3996436, 7270253, CC BY 4.0). I found no repository dataset that pairs shell morphometrics with genotype for the same Peneroplis or soritid specimens, and the morphometric sets are planktonic, not Peneroplis. WoRMS gives the name list for Peneroplis (34 children on its first page).
next_step: Pull Peneroplis/soritid SSU accessions with voucher or morphotype fields from GenBank and match them to the species names in WoRMS; for morphometrics compile shell images from the source papers, or use the planktonic sets as a restricted-scope test.
obstacles_confirmed: Peneroplis has far less public genetic and culture data than planktonic globigerinids.
Type material and sequence records are rarely linked to the same individuals.
Genetic barcoding covers only a fraction of described foraminiferal morphospecies.
